James Joyce, Exiles.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/james-joyce/exiles

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- James Joyce, the author, died 1941 (Wikidata Q6882, P570 = 1941-01-13).

First publication of the text used: 1918 (SE colophon: 'Exiles was published in 1918 by James Joyce.'). The Wikipedia infobox gives the country as Ireland and the first publication as Grant Richards, 25 May 1918.

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in 1918, before 1931, so the US rule settles its origin too. A published work enters the United States public domain 95 years after publication, so this work entered it in 2013.
- Country of origin (Ireland, per the Wikipedia infobox): copyright there lasts for life plus 70 years after the death of the last surviving person named above. The last to die did so in 1941, so the work is in the public domain there since 1 January 2012. The United Kingdom uses the same term.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."

Sources of these facts:
- SE colophon: 'Exiles was published in 1918 by James Joyce.'
- Wikidata Q6882 (James Joyce), P570 = 1941-01-13
